title: Universal closedness tested by normal finite-type curves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $g:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact $k$-morphism. The following three conditions are equivalent.

(1) $g$ is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism].

(2) For every integer $n\geq0$, the map $1\times g:\mathbf A^n_k\times_k X\to\mathbf A^n_k\times_k Y$ is closed on underlying topological spaces, where $\mathbf A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and the products are fibre products [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-fibre-product].

(3) Let $C$ be any integral scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] such that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $c\in C$ be closed with $\dim\mathcal O_{C,c}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], put $U=C\setminus\{c\}$, $R=\mathcal O_{C,c}$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$. For every pair of $k$-morphisms $a:U\to X$ and $b:C\to Y$ with $ga=b|_U$, there exists a $k$-morphism $h:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ such that $gh=b|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ and $h|_{\operatorname{Spec}F}=a|_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$. The restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ uses the canonical map from the spectrum of a local ring [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]; the generic map is its restriction along $R\hookrightarrow F$. No uniqueness, separatedness, or reducedness assumption is made on $g$, $X$, or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0GWV (limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed), equivalence (1)--(3), specialized to S=Spec k; fields are Nagata by algebra.tex Tag 0335 (algebra-proposition-ubiquity-nagata), item (1).

proof.text: (1) implies (2): $1\times g$ is the base change of $g$ along $\mathbf A^n_k\times_kY\to Y$, as seen by pairing the two components in the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. It is closed by the definition of universal closedness [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, proof, specialized to Spec k.

proof.text: Assume (2). Closedness is local on the target, so to verify universal closedness work over an affine open $S=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$; its source $X_S$ is quasi-compact over $S$ by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. Take any $T\to S$ and closed subset $D\subseteq X_S\times_ST$. If its image $E$ is not closed, choose $t\in\overline E\setminus E$ and give $D$ its reduced closed-subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Apply [lem-sfb-missing-fibre-finite-presentation-approximation] to this closed subscheme and $t$. It supplies $V,a:T\supset V\to T\prime,Z\prime$ with empty fibre at $a(t)$ and $a(E\cap V)\subseteq\operatorname{image}(Z\prime\to T\prime)$. Continuity and $t\in\overline{E\cap V}$ imply that $a(t)$ lies in the closure of this latter image. But the displayed polynomial quotient for $T\prime$ gives a closed immersion $T\prime\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_S$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its base change on sources is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], so $Z\prime$ is a closed subset of $\mathbf A^r_S\times_SX_S$. Condition (2), restricted to $\mathbf A^r_S$, makes its image closed there, hence closed in the subspace $T\prime$. That image omits $a(t)$ by the empty-fibre assertion, a contradiction. Thus every $E$ is closed; the affine opens $S$ cover every base change, proving (1).

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, proof, specialized to Spec k.

proof.text: Assume (1) and take a test $C,c,R,F,a,b$ from (3). Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $B$ is finitely generated over $k$, hence Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], $R\cong B_{\mathfrak p}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $R$ Noetherian. It is a normal local domain of dimension one by the test hypotheses, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes it a DVR, hence a valuation ring by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The generic map from $\operatorname{Spec}F$ lands in $U$, since it maps to the generic point of the positive-dimensional integral $C$. Apply [lem-sfb-universally-closed-valuative-existence] to $a|_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$ and $b|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$. Their square commutes because $ga=b|_U$. Its lift is exactly the $h$ required by (3).

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, proof, specialized to Spec k.

proof.text: Assume (3). Its extension property is preserved by products with $\mathbf A^n_k$: write a test map to $\mathbf A^n_k\times Y$ as $(b_0,b_1)$, apply (3) to the $X$-component of the punctured map and $b_1$, and pair the resulting lift with $b_0|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$. The generic restrictions agree componentwise. The same property is inherited by $g_V:g^{-1}(V)\to V$ for an open $V\subseteq Y$: compose a test with the inclusions, apply (3), and factor the lift through $g^{-1}(V)$ since its composite with $g$ equals the given map into $V$. These factorizations are the defining universal property of open inverse images and fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, proof, specialized to Spec k.

proof.text: For each $n$, put $g_n=1\times g$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. Its source and target are locally of finite type over $k$: on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$ or $Y$, $B$ is finitely generated over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]; the polynomial ring $B[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ is generated by those generators and $t_1,\ldots,t_n$. Equivalently, the product over this chart is finite type by base change of $\mathbf A^n_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and composition, [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. To show $g_n$ is closed it suffices to work over each affine open $V$ of its target: for a closed subset $Z$ of its source, the image intersected with $V$ equals the image of the relatively closed subset $Z\cap g_n^{-1}(V)$. The restricted map $f:g_n^{-1}(V)\to V$ remains quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], and inherits (3) by step 4.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, proof, specialized to Spec k.

proof.text: Fix such $f:X_V\to V$ and a closed subset $Z\subseteq X_V$. Suppose $f(Z)$ is not closed. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-image-immediate-boundary-point]. Step 5 supplies exactly its affine-target, local-finite-type and quasi-compactness hypotheses. Obtain $y\notin f(Z)$, $t$, $x\in Z$, the integral affine $T=\overline{\{t\}}$ of finite type, its closed point $y$ of local dimension one, and the finite extension $L=\kappa(x)/K$ with $K=\kappa(t)$. The node also supplies the generic map $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X_V$ over $T\hookrightarrow V$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-curve-punctured-generic-model] with $W=X_V$, $Y=V$ and $i:T\hookrightarrow V$. All its hypotheses, including the exact generic compatibility, have now been supplied. Obtain $C,c,p,a$ and put $b=i p:C\to V$. Then $b(c)=y$, $fa=b|_{C\setminus\{c\}}$, and the generic image of $a$ is $x$.

source.place: Tag 0GWV, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-universally-closed, proof, specialized to Spec k.

proof.text: Apply the inherited condition (3) for $f$ to this $C,c,a,b$. The model node ensures that $C$ is integral and finite type over $k$, all its local rings are integrally closed domains, $c$ is closed, and $\dim\mathcal O_{C,c}=1$. Thus it gives $h:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{C,c}\to X_V$ over $b$ agreeing with $a$ generically. Its generic point maps to $x\in Z$. By continuity, $h^{-1}(Z)$ is a closed subset containing the generic point of the spectrum of this domain; it is therefore the entire spectrum. In particular its closed point maps into $Z$. The canonical local-spectrum morphism sends that closed point to $c$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], so its image under $f h$ is $b(c)=y$. This contradicts $y\notin f(Z)$. Hence all these restricted maps are closed, then all $g_n$ are closed by step 5. Condition (2) follows and step 2 gives (1). No uniqueness of a lift or extension to the whole of $C$ is used.
